top.line: A proposal to news editors: more revenue from the read, not the subscription, with free client-side code.
top.para: And the associations to talk to.

in-short.line: Journalism is a business; subscriptions hit a ceiling; micropayments failed; pay by the read; not proven yet.

business.line: Around 300 UK local titles closed since 2005; 171 of 308 Portuguese municipalities at risk.
business.para: Local journalism is the heart of it.

subscriptions.line: About 10% pay for online news in the UK, 8% in Portugal; most say they never will.
subscriptions.para: One article, three subscriptions, nothing paid.

lessons.line: Blendle, Coil, Axate and Google's Offerwall: friction sank the early ones; agents are a new reader.

model.line: £5 of credit, a few pence a page, charged by the share read, never blocked, all in the browser.
model.para: Free for any publisher; PrompTugal.news runs it.

ways.line: The meter, a revenue share via PrompTugal.news, licences to quote, agents paying at the source.
ways.para: Provenance says whose story it is.

workflow.line: One regional story read on its own site and carried by PrompTugal.news, a share paid back.

proof.line: Not proven: our revenue is small because our traffic is; we need partners with readers.

associations.line: NMA, ICNN, PINF and the Society of Editors; API, AIIC, APMEDIO and ERC; News Media Europe and others.

limits.line: Not proven at scale; the revenue share is a proposal; others' figures as reported.

sources.line: Press Gazette, PINF, LabCom, Reuters Institute, Piano, TollBit and others, and earlier articles.
